newsitem.title: USA: NAPM's Ore not worried by rise in price component.
newsitem.headline: NAPM's Ore not worried by rise in price component.

text.p: The increase in the price component of the January National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index was not worrisome, NAPM Business Survey Committee Chairman Norbert Ore said.
"The increase was only a minor increase," Ore told a teleconference following the release of the NAPM's monthly index of business activity.
"So, I would not see that as an indicator at this point (of inflationary pressures)," he added.
He noted that 75 percent of NAPM members are still reporting prices are the same.
The NAPM price component rose to 51.4 in January from 50.8 in December.
Although Ore played down the importance of the rise in the price component, he noted that energy prices are "strong" because of seasonal as well as supply and demand factors.
Turning to the outlook for trade, Ore pointed out that exports and imports are still growing.
When asked what impact further gains in the dollar would have on trade, Ore said, "That would obviously have an impact on our export and import position ..."
The NAPM manufacturing activity index fell to 52.0 in January from a revised 53.8 in December.
Ore said the index at 52.0 is equal to 2.8 percent growth in gross domestic product.
